diagnostic_evidence.quote:
So, for $|\|\mat{A}_{k}^{\vx}\vx\|_2^2 - \|\vx\|_2|^2 \leq \delta$ with probability at least $\alpha > 0$, we would need
$$ m \geq C^d \delta^{-2} \ln(4/\alpha),$$
for some new constant $C>0$. The desired result follows by the union bound argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 3.2 (Rico et al., 2022) guarantees deviation at most $\delta$ with failure probability at most $\beta$ only when $k_2 = \ln(8/\beta)$ rows are trimmed. In the proof of Lemma 3.2, for a single vector $\vx_i$, setting $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$ yields a failure probability bounded only by $\alpha$. To guarantee that the bound holds simultaneously for all $p$ vectors via a union bound with total failure probability at most $\alpha$, each vector must have an individual failure probability at most $\alpha/p$, which requires trimming $k = \ln(8p/\alpha)$ rows. Fixing $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$ independently of $p$ leaves each marginal failure probability at $\alpha$, so the union bound only yields a trivial failure probability bound of $p\alpha$. Downstream, Theorem 4 applies Lemma 3.2 over an $\varepsilon$-net $\mathcal{N}$ of size $\exp(\Omega(dnr))$ with $k = \ln(8n^\phi)$, where the union bound failure probability $|\mathcal{N}|n^{-\phi}$ diverges to infinity.

failure_location.quote:
Further, for any finite set $\{\tX_1, \ldots, \tX_p\} = \mathcal{S} \subseteq \R^{n \times n \times \dots \times n}$,  we consider their embedding with respect to the data-driven row trimming of $\mat{A}^{\vx_i}_k$ with $\vx_i = \algoname{Vec}(\tX_i)$ and $k = \ln(8/\alpha)$,

with probability at least $1 - \alpha$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must set $k = \ln(8p/\alpha)$ in Lemma 3.2 and establish that trimming a number of rows $k$ that scales with the metric entropy of low-rank tensor classes preserves the geometry uniformly without discarding a substantial fraction of the $m$ measurements.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 fails for multi-point sets whenever $p > 1/\alpha$. As a direct consequence, Theorem 4 (and informal Theorem 1), which claims uniform norm preservation over all low-rank tensors by trimming only $k = \ln(8n^\phi)$ rows from face-splitting measurements, is unproven and invalid.
issues.title: Invalid union bound in Lemma 3.2 fixes trimming parameter k independently of point set size p
issues.why_classification: Theorem 4 is the central theoretical result of Section 3 and an advertised main contribution of the paper. Repairing it would require fundamentally altering the trimming budget $k$ or developing a new proof architecture for uniform geometry preservation of face-splitting measurements that avoids the union bound over nets.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $y_i = \va_i^T \vx$, and $|y_{i_1}| \leq |y_{i_2}| \leq \dots \le |y_{i_m}|$, let $i_1, i_2, \dots, i_{m-k}$ be all the first $m-k$ indices. 
Then, the $j$-th row of the trimmed matrix $\mat{A}_k^\vx \in \R^{ (m - k) \times n}$  is given by
$$ \sqrt\frac{{m}}{m-k} \va_{i_j} \quad j \in [m-k]\;.$$

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm 1, the trimming budget $m_{\text{trim}}$ is the number of rows to be removed (e.g., $m_{\text{trim}} \in [5, 80]$ while $m = 1000$). However, Line 4 defines $\Theta_k = [i_1, \dots, i_{m_{\text{trim}}}]$, which selects only the first $m_{\text{trim}}$ indices corresponding to the smallest residuals. Consequently, the algorithm retains only $m_{\text{trim}}$ rows and discards the remaining $m - m_{\text{trim}}$ rows, directly contradicting Definition 3.1 and equation (12), where $\mat{A}_k$ is scaled by $\sqrt{m / (m - m_{\text{trim}})}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change Line 4 of Algorithm 1 to $\Theta_k = [i_1, i_2, \dots, i_{m - m_{\text{trim}}}]$.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm 1 as written executes gradient steps using only a tiny fraction of the measurements ($m_{\text{trim}}$ rather than $m - m_{\text{trim}}$), causing extreme data loss and a scaling mismatch with the intended trimmed loss function.
issues.title: Index slicing in Algorithm 1 retains trimmed rows instead of remaining measurements
issues.why_classification: The repair is a straightforward local correction of the index slice from $m_{\text{trim}}$ to $m - m_{\text{trim}}$, which immediately aligns the pseudocode with equation (12) and Definition 3.1 without altering any proofs or results.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement of Theorem 5 claims that the residual at iteration $t+1$ satisfies $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \le (\alpha_t)^{t+1} \|\tR^0\|_F$. However, the proof only establishes the one-step inequality $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \le \alpha_t \|\tR^t\|_F$. Because the contraction factor $\alpha_t$ depends on iteration-specific quantities ($\mu_t, \rho_t, \Delta_t, \xi_t, \mat{A}_t$), unrolling the recurrence over $t+1$ steps produces $\prod_{s=0}^t \alpha_s \|\tR^0\|_F$, which is not equal to $(\alpha_t)^{t+1} \|\tR^0\|_F$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the bound in the statement of Theorem 5 with the one-step inequality $\|\tR^{t+1}\|_F \le \alpha_t \|\tR^t\|_F$, or state the unrolled bound as $\left(\prod_{s=0}^t \alpha_s\right) \|\tR^0\|_F$.
issues.overall_effect: The stated multi-step contraction rate in equation (13) of Theorem 5 is mathematically unsupported as written whenever the iterate-dependent parameters vary across iterations.
issues.title: Theorem 5 asserts an unrolled power rate with iterate-dependent contraction parameters
issues.why_classification: The one-step contraction proved in the text is valid, and stating the one-step contraction or product over time steps preserves the intended message and subsequent discussion (such as equation (15)) without requiring new proof architecture.
